query: For additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components, what single intervention could improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity while reducing fabrication-induced defects? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the current fabrication baseline, defines the processing and application conditions under which it should hold, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Optimizing laser powder bed fusion process parameters, specifically by reducing the laser power from 200 W to 150 W and increasing the scanning speed from 500 mm/s to 700 mm/s, will improve the dimensional precision and mechanical integrity of additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components while reducing fabrication-induced defects.
generation.material_initial_state: as-fabricated high-entropy-alloy components with potential defects
generation.intervention: optimization of laser powder bed fusion process parameters
generation.conditions: laser power: 150 W, scanning speed: 700 mm/s, layer thickness: 30 μm, and build orientation: 0°
generation.mechanism: the optimized process parameters reduce the energy input and increase the cooling rate, resulting in a more uniform microstructure and reduced defects
generation.predicted_outcome: improvement in dimensional precision by 15% and mechanical integrity by 20%, and reduction in fabrication-induced defects by 30%
generation.baseline: current fabrication baseline with laser power: 200 W and scanning speed: 500 mm/s
generation.boundary: applicable to high-entropy-alloy components fabricated using laser powder bed fusion with a layer thickness of 30 μm and build orientation of 0°
generation.uncertainty: the actual improvement may vary depending on the specific high-entropy-alloy composition and the desired application conditions

falsification_experiment.design: fabricate high-entropy-alloy components using the optimized process parameters and measure their dimensional precision, mechanical integrity, and defect density
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: if the measured improvement in dimensional precision is less than 10% or the measured improvement in mechanical integrity is less than 15%, or the measured reduction in fabrication-induced defects is less than 20%, then the hypothesis is falsified
